text: Scientists call this eruption modest. It closed more than three hundred airports.
This is Eyjafjallajökull, in Iceland, in 2010.
In one week that April, airports across Europe closed, in about two dozen countries.
More than a hundred thousand flights were cancelled, and seven million passengers were affected.
Its plumes were three to ten kilometres high, with about a quarter of a cubic kilometre of airborne ash.
On the official scale, that's a level four.
So how many levels are above this one? That's in the full video, and it's linked right here.
